construct: The false discovery rate is the expected proportion of false positives among hypotheses declared significant. The Benjamini-Hochberg step-up procedure controls FDR and generally retains greater power than procedures such as Bonferroni correction that control the family-wise probability of any false-positive result.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The stated goal is to control the expected proportion of false positives among declared significant results in a high-dimensional setting; that is FDR control, classically by Benjamini-Hochberg.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Bonferroni appropriately addresses multiplicity but controls family-wise error and is more conservative than the stated target; it does not match the requested error metric.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The wording explicitly defines FDR, so Benjamini-Hochberg is the single best method.
